autoChain.maxLatencyHelp: Default 1000 ms. Switch only after 3 slow checks and a faster backup; keep healthy routes.
autoChain.allSources: All subscriptions (include newly added subscriptions automatically)
autoChain.title: Auto Chain
autoChain.description: Choose a fixed exit and relay subscriptions, then enable automatic testing, connection and relay switching.
autoChain.target: Traffic group to use this chain
autoChain.hint: Probe the current route and up to two backups every 2 seconds after each round, with a 5-second timeout. Fail over after 2 consecutive failures. Full scans run at most 4 probes concurrently and repeat after the configured interval, including during outages. Slow-route switches have a 30-second cooldown; failures bypass it. Existing connections may need to reconnect.
autoChain.recovering: No healthy route yet. Probing continues automatically.
autoChain.notSelected: Loading the automatic chain; connection will start automatically.
autoChain.unavailable: Cannot read live core status. Last results may be outdated.
autoChain.loadFailed: Unable to load subscription nodes. Reopen to retry.
autoChain.directMode: Switch to Rule or Global mode before connecting the automatic chain.
autoChain.route: This device → Automatic relay → Your exit → Website
autoChain.routeHint: Relays are tested and switched automatically. The final hop stays on your chosen exit node.
autoChain.exitHelp: For example, choose your Japan residential node to use its public IP, rather than choosing the Hong Kong relay here.
autoChain.targetHelp: Only traffic assigned to “{{group}}” will use this chain. This choice does not affect test results.
autoChain.toleranceHelp: Compare this difference only after sustained high latency. A faster backup does not replace a healthy route.
autoChain.summary: Uses rule mode. Existing direct and reject decisions stay intact; proxy traffic, Claude connections and protected-domain DNS use the fixed-exit chain. Existing connections reconnect. Unavailable relays are retried without direct fallback.
autoChain.sourcesHelp: All subscriptions includes future additions, or select sources manually. Identical connections are deduplicated with all sources shown. The fixed exit is excluded from relays.
autoChain.progress: Results since this configuration loaded: {{completed}} / {{total}} routes
autoChain.resultsHint: Latency includes local → relay → fixed exit → HTTPS handshakes and response. Reachability applies only to the test URL. Failures may come from either hop or the 5-second timeout. Full scans use up to 4 concurrent probes; current and backup checks run separately.
autoChain.noResults: No matching nodes. Check selected subscriptions and available nodes.
autoChain.initialScan: Running the initial full-route scan. Results appear as each test completes…
autoChain.noCandidates: No candidate routes: check that the exit still exists and the subscriptions contain other eligible relay nodes.

claudeGuard.title: Claude exit protection
claudeGuard.description: Claude processes and the listed domains prefer JP-REALITY-SOCKS, whose server supplies the fixed exit. Existing .92 SOCKS exits remain supported when this node is absent. Other sites keep their routing.
claudeGuard.route: Claude / DNS → protected exit group → JP-REALITY-SOCKS or fixed .92 SOCKS → destination
claudeGuard.verified: Fixed-exit candidates loaded. Public egress and OS filtering have not been attested.
claudeGuard.blocked: Fixed exit missing or core unavailable. Claude cannot fall back to other exits.
claudeGuard.boundary: No port 17891 gateway required. System bypass prevention needs separately installed and verified filters. This page does not attest those filters. Unknown third-party domains are outside domain routing coverage.
claudeGuard.mode: Windows protection requires rule mode across profiles. LAN requests go through local Clash and then DIRECT; localhost remains accessible. A missing protected exit blocks Claude.
